examples.before:
# team config
model: opus  # default model
retry: 3
examples.input: `TROUPE_ACTOR=robot:x config set model sonnet --reason try`, then `TROUPE_ACTOR=human:owner config history`

results.1: The set exits 2 with the actor error and leaves the file unchanged. The history call then exits 0 and lists only the two original import entries (model = "opus" and retry = 3, actor unknown), with no record of the failed set. Same in all six arms.

context.in_practice: There is only one route here, and all six arms behaved the same way: a malformed `TROUPE_ACTOR` stops every command (get, set and history) with exit 2 before it does anything. Only the wording of the error message differs between arms. Once the variable is fixed, everything works normally.
context.stakes: If `TROUPE_ACTOR` holds a bad value, a user wants to find out right away, on any command, and not only when a write goes into the history under a garbage name. The flip side is that a bad value also blocks plain reads.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 catches a bad actor value straight away and never writes anything with it, but the cost is that read-only commands like `get` and `history` also refuse to run until the variable is fixed.

plan_why: Shows that an invalid TROUPE_ACTOR is rejected with exit 2 by every command (read-only get/history too) and before anything else (before the import, before a path-not-found error, before set writes), and that nothing was recorded or written as a result
